title: CLAIM: A 'stand down' order was issued at Benghazi
summary: The House Select Committee (2016) found NO stand-down order was issued, and that US forces in Europe could not have arrived in time — consistent with all prior inquiries.
tldr: The claim that a 'stand down' order was issued at Benghazi is not substantiated: the CIA Chief of Base testified under oath that he told no one to stand down, and the committee found U.S. military assets simply never reached Benghazi in time.
ai_summary:
AI review of the Wikipedia overview article "United States House Select Committee on Benghazi," read in full:
- Committee basics: created by House vote 232–186 on May 8, 2014, chaired by Trey Gowdy with ranking Democrat Elijah Cummings; $3.3 million budget; final report released June 28, 2016; committee closed December 12, 2016.
- Military response: the article reports the committee's finding that "No U.S. military asset was ever deployed to Benghazi despite the order of the Secretary of Defense at 7 o'clock that night," and that forces reached Benghazi only by mid-afternoon the day after the attack.
- Clinton findings: Clinton testified for over eight hours on October 22, 2015; "The report itself found no wrongdoing by Hillary Clinton," while Democrats acknowledged "security measures in Benghazi were woefully inadequate."
- Politicization context: Kevin McCarthy's September 2015 Hannity admission that the committee drove Clinton's poll numbers down; committee staffer Bradley Podliska's wrongful-termination suit alleging a partisan investigation; the NYT editorial board's October 2015 call to shut the committee down after it spent $4.6 million.
- Source caveat: this Wikipedia overview contains ZERO mentions of the word "stand down" — it does not report the specific no-stand-down finding. That finding comes from the underlying H. Rept. 114-848 (reviewed under the benghazi-report record), where the CIA Chief of Base testified, "I did not, I did not tell anybody to stand down" and "I did not issue a stand-down order." The record summary is consistent with the underlying report but not fully verifiable from this primary source alone.
